issues.description: Constructor parameter mismatch: The constructor StockIngredient(String name, int price, int quantity) is declared in the problem UML and used in examples (e.g., Main) and the solution, but the template only provides a StockIngredient constructor with signature StockIngredient(String name, int price, int quantity, boolean strictValidation). Because the three-argument constructor is missing in the template, students cannot instantiate StockIngredient using the expected three-parameter form (this causes compilation failures where the three-argument form is used and contradicts the UML and solution).
issues.suggestedFix: Restore or add an overloaded three-argument constructor with signature StockIngredient(String name, int price, int quantity) in the template so it matches the UML and solution. Implement it to perform the same validation/assignments as the solution (or delegate to the existing four-argument constructor, e.g., this(name, price, quantity, false)), ensuring students can instantiate StockIngredient with three arguments as shown in examples.

issues.description: Constructor signature mismatch for the StockIngredient concept: the problem statement (class diagram) and the solution implementation expect a 3-argument constructor StockIngredient(String name, int price, int quantity), but the template provides a 4-argument constructor StockIngredient(String name, int price, int quantity, boolean strictValidation). This discrepancy prevents a direct mapping between the exercise specification and the template: students and tests will expect to call new StockIngredient(name, price, quantity) (as described in the problem and shown in the solution), but the template does not declare that 3-arg constructor, which is likely to confuse students or cause compilation errors when following the instructions.
issues.suggestedFix: Provide the expected 3-argument constructor in the template. Add an overloaded constructor with signature public StockIngredient(String name, int price, int quantity) that delegates to the existing implementation (for example: this(name, price, quantity, true);) so the template matches the problem statement and solution. Alternatively, replace the 4-argument constructor with the 3-argument version used in the problem statement and solution.
